newsitem.title: USA: Energy Dept sees $80 hike in new refrigerator price.
newsitem.headline: Energy Dept sees $80 hike in new refrigerator price.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department said Wednesday that its new rule calling for 30 percent more energy savings from refrigerators would boost store prices for refrigerators by $80.
Energy Secretary Federico Pena unveiled the new refrigerator standard, saying it would be "good for the environment and good for consumers' pocketbooks."
"The annual energy savings for consumers will top $1 billion in 2010, and over $2 billion in 2020," he said.

Refrigerator makers had said it would cost them about $70 per unit more to produce the new models by July 2001, which could in turn result in a $160 increase in the average store price for refrigerators.
However, they added that because the market was so competitive among manufacturers and mega-retailers, consumers were unlikely to see the higher prices.

According to Energy Department estimates, redesigning refrigerators to meet the higher energy-efficiency standard would cost manufacturers only $40 per unit, which would result in an $80 hike at the retail level above today's average of $600.
